correctness.rationale: Ranks 1–4 distinguish the vertices of every strict chain, so stabilizers fix chain simplices pointwise and face deletion in rank order gives the ordinary quotient cellular differential. Independently ran /workspace/reviews/replay5.py (Python 3 + SymPy): generate noncrossing partitions via Dyck words, verify noncrossing and completeness against the Catalan count, generate all refinement chains by block containment, and enumerate orbits by the rotation and reflection generators. Labelled and quotient f-vectors are (130,1035,2160,1296) and (22,114,204,116). The integer matrices compose to zero; their Smith forms have 21, 93 and 111 nonzero invariant factors, all units. Consequently the images are primitive, the homology is torsion free, and its ranks are 1,0,0,5. Shellability and purity give a simply connected labeled complex; the reflections i→−i and i→1−i fix the vertices with sole nonsingleton blocks {1,5} and {0,1}, and their product gives a rotation generating the cyclic part. Armstrong therefore gives trivial quotient fundamental group. Hurewicz twice gives pi_2=0 and pi_3=Z^5; five sphere representatives give an integral homology isomorphism, hence a homotopy equivalence by the simply connected Whitehead theorem. This is not a homeomorphism, equivariant result, or statement about a quotient graph; the homology computation alone would not prove it. Supplied checker inspected, not run.

value.rationale: The hexagon is the first size at which cyclic and dihedral vertex orbit counts differ, motivating the quotient and the size before computing homology. Establishing the complete integral homotopy type goes beyond those counts, and distinguishes a wedge of five spheres from spaces with the same rational rank but torsion or nontrivial fundamental group. This is a natural small quotient whose precise topology is useful in comparing symmetry actions on partition complexes.
